rationale: Developers and sysadmins want a polished TUI network monitor, but this is a developer tooling problem that requires systems-level code (kernel socket inspection, ncurses/ratatui TUI) — not something Claude prompts and a web form can build. Willingness to pay is near zero: the entire category of CLI monitoring tools is open-source and free (nethogs, iftop, jnettop), and developers strongly resist paying for tools in this space. The buyer is identifiable (sysadmin/dev) but has no established budget for this category.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. This requires a native systems-programming tool (Rust/Go/C with kernel-level socket access and a terminal UI framework) — completely outside what Claude prompts and simple web pages can produce. The operator cannot build this without a developer writing code. Additionally, the target buyers do not pay for CLI tools — they use free open-source alternatives or build their own. Drop this opportunity.
